title.en: Hawaii braces for potential first direct hit by a hurricane in 34 years
title.zh: 夏威夷正准备迎接 34 年来首次飓风直接袭击

summary.en: In a worst-case scenario, category one Lala could dump up to 25in (63cm) of rain on Big Island.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Hawaii is bracing for what could be its first direct hit from a hurricane since 1992, as category one storm Lala churns off its coast.

Packing 75mph (120km/h) winds, Lala gained hurricane strength on Saturday. In a worst-case scenario, it could dump up to 25in (63cm) of rain on Big Island and produce a 3ft storm surge.

A hurricane warning is in effect for Big Island, while Maui County, Oahu, Kauai and Niihau are under a tropical storm warnings. Officials have told residents to prepare for "life-threatening" conditions, including floods and mudslides.

The storm is expected to either make landfall or pass close to the southern tip of Big Island on Saturday, before continuing west.

The last time a hurricane made landfall on Hawaii's Big Island was 155 years ago, according to the Associated Press news agency.

Over the weekend, Lala will continue moving westwards, and may weaken into a tropical storm, with the centre passing just below Hawaii's other islands.

Hawaii Governor Josh Green warned residents to brace for "an incredible amount of water".

He said on X: "Damaging winds, heavy rain, flash flooding and dangerous surf are possible across the state through the weekend."

At Ellison Onizuka Kona International - Big Island's largest airport - 40% of flights were grounded, according to flightaware.com. Some 80% of flights were called off at its other main airport, Hilo International.

The more dire forecasts from the National Weather Service (NWS) have been issued for areas within Big Island's south-east.

"Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues," the NWS said, adding that rivers and tributaries "may rapidly overflow their banks in multiple places".

Local message boards on Facebook show residents filling bags with sand to protect their homes and inquiring whether stores remained open in the early hours on Saturday.

Hawaii County's Civil Defense Agency said public shelters were available in every county on Big Island.

"At this time, you should have completed your storm-ready preparations and focusing on your Sheltering Plan," the agency said on X.

Iniki, a powerful category four storm, was the last hurricane to strike Hawaii back in 1992.

It caused six deaths and $3bn in damage after making landfall on the southern coast of Kauai.

Hurricane season in the US has been relatively quiet the last few years - the last major storm was category three Hurricane Milton, which hit Florida in October 2024.

The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration has said that 2026 might be another low-frequency year for hurricanes in the US, predicting , external a 55% chance of a below-normal season.

title.en: Rescuers search for survivors of powerful Indonesia earthquake
title.zh: 救援人员搜寻印度尼西亚强烈地震的幸存者

summary.en: Officials say a rapid assessment into the impact of the earthquake that destroyed hundreds of buildings and killed 47 is under way.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Rescue teams in Indonesia have been searching for survivors of Saturday's major earthquake which left at least 47 people dead.

The magnitude 7.7 quake struck the island of Flores shortly before 05:00 (22:00 GMT on Friday) and had a depth of 15km, Indonesia's meteorology and geophysics agency stated.

Preliminary reports indicate hundreds of buildings have been severely damaged by the quake and the dozens of aftershocks that followed.

However, the full scale of the disaster is still unclear, and news of a second earthquake of magnitude 6.9 at the other end of Indonesia served as a reminder of why they call this region the ring of fire.

Tremors from Saturday's powerful earthquake were reportedly felt by residents as far west as Bima Regency and City, the National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) agency said, but the Manggarai province is among the most affected.

Preliminary data shows that 24 fatalities had been recorded there, meanwhile 17 deaths were recorded in East Manggarai province, three in Sikka province, and at least one in each of the Ngada, Ende and West Manggarai provinces.

The BNPB said aid was being sent to the affected areas with 10,500 packages arriving at the base operations so far.

It will take time to assess the full extent of the destruction in the region, which is remote and mountainous.

However, early reports indicate more than 150 houses had been severely damaged, as well as dozens of educational institutions, a number of healthcare facilities, places of worship, offices, and several other public facilities.

Video taken at the port in Maumere - the largest town in Flores - showed large chunks of concrete breaking off the terminal building onto passengers waiting to board an inter-island ferry. Some were thrown into the sea when the gangway to a ship collapsed.

Emanuel Melkiades Laka Lena, governor of East Nusa Tenggara province, told a news conference that they were killed in their sleep by collapsing rubble.

Others, like Arnold Welianto, who lives in Talibura, a village near the coastline in Sikka, East Nusa Tenggara, were shaken out of their beds.

He also told the BBC that many people had already fled into the hills because the sea had also receded.

While a tsunami warning was initially issued - leading some 2,000 people to self-evacuate - it was lifted around three hours after the initial jolt, when no significant sea level rise was detected.

Landslides, however, did block access to some villages but the experienced rescue teams worked tirelessly through the day to free those trapped under the rubble.

In Ruteng, a temporary medical tent was also assembled outside of a hospital to treat earthquake victims.

body.zh: 印度尼西亚的救援队一直在寻找星期六大地震的幸存者，这场地震造成至少 47 人死亡。 印度尼西亚气象和地球物理机构表示，在 05:00（格林威治标准时间周五 22:00）前不久，弗洛勒斯岛发生了 7.7 级地震，震源深度为 15 公里。 初步报告显示，数百座建筑物在地震和随后发生的数十次余震中严重受损。 然而，灾难的全面规模仍不清楚，印度尼西亚另一端发生第二次6.9级地震的消息提醒人们为什么他们称该地区为火环。 国家灾害管理局（BNPB）表示，据报道，远至西边的比马县和市的居民都感受到了周六强烈地震带来的震动，但芒加莱省是受影响最严重的省份之一。 初步数据显示，该地区已造成 24 人死亡，同时东芒加莱省有 17 人死亡，锡卡省有 3 人死亡，恩加达省、恩德省和西芒加莱省各至少有 1 人死亡。 BNPB 表示，目前已有 10,500 个包裹抵达基地，援助物资正在运往受影响地区。 该地区地处偏远、山区，需要时间来评估其破坏的全部范围。 然而，早期报告显示，150 多所房屋以及数十个教育机构、一些医疗设施、礼拜场所、办公室和其他一些公共设施遭到严重损坏。 在弗洛勒斯最大城镇毛梅雷的港口拍摄的视频显示，航站楼上有大块混凝土脱落，砸在等待登上岛际渡轮的乘客身上。当一艘船的舷梯倒塌时，一些人被扔进海里。 东努沙登加拉省省长伊曼纽尔·梅尔基亚德斯·拉卡·莱纳在新闻发布会上说，他们在睡梦中被倒塌的瓦砾炸死。 其他人，比如住在东努沙登加拉省锡卡海岸线附近塔利布拉村的阿诺德·韦利安托(Arnold Welianto)，都被从床上摇了起来。 他还告诉BBC，由于海水也退去了，许多人已经逃进山里。 虽然最初发布了海啸警报，导致约 2,000 人自行疏散，但在最初的震动大约三个小时后解除，当时没有检测到海平面明显上升。 然而，山体滑坡确实封锁了通往一些村庄的道路，但经验丰富的救援队全天不知疲倦地工作，以解救被困在废墟下的人们。 在如腾，医院外还搭建了临时医疗帐篷，用于救治地震灾民。 BNPB 持续建议人们保持冷静，远离沿海地区……

title.en: Australian state to launch gun buyback after Bondi Beach attack
title.zh: 邦迪海滩袭击后澳大利亚各州启动枪支回购

summary.en: New South Wales, where the attack took place, will offer gun owners cash to give up their firearms.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australia's most populous state will launch a gun buyback scheme later this year, becoming the first to offer cash in exchange for firearms in the wake of the Bondi Beach terror attack.

Gun owners in New South Wales (NSW) will be offered up to AUS$1,000 (£523) to hand over eligible handguns, shotguns and rifles from 2 November.

Australian authorities had pledged sweeping firearm law reforms after 15 people were shot dead at a Jewish festival on Sydney's Bondi Beach, which is located in NSW, last December.

The state's premier Chris Minns said on Saturday: "We want those guns handed in, compensated for and safely destroyed."

Gun ownership reforms already introduced by the state mean individuals can only own four firearms - although some people, such as farmers and sports shooters, can own a maximum of 10.

The scheme will be offered to those who have more weapons than permitted by the new rules, or who are no longer covered by a licence - with terms having been reduced from five years to two.

The scheme will be implemented in two phases. The first - from the start of November - covers types of handguns, shotguns and rifles.

Those handing over a revolver, for example, will be paid AUS$1,000, while an air rifle will fetch AUS$450.

The second phase will begin early next year and cover "higher-value firearms" valued above AUS$3,000, capped at AUS$10,000.

The National Gun BuyBack Scheme is being jointly funded by New South Wales and the federal government.

Businesses will be able to receive up to AUS$25,000 in support to help them adjust to the reforms, with help also offered to gun-dealers.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said: "We must do everything we can to make sure the antisemitic terrorist attack in Bondi doesn't happen again.

On 14 December last year, 15 people including a 10-year-old girl and a Holocaust survivor were killed as Hanukkah celebrations took place near Australia's most famous beach.

Australian authorities had initially planned a nationwide gun buyback, though plans have been delayed over funding and how it would be implemented.
body.zh: 澳大利亚人口最多的州将于今年晚些时候推出枪支回购计划，成为邦迪海滩恐怖袭击后第一个提供现金换取枪支的州。 从 11 月 2 日起，新南威尔士州 (NSW) 的枪支拥有者将获得高达 1,000 澳元（523 英镑）的补贴，以交出符合条件的手枪、霰弹枪和步枪。 去年 12 月，在新南威尔士州悉尼邦迪海滩的犹太节日上有 15 人被枪杀后，澳大利亚当局承诺对枪支法进行全面改革。 该州州长克里斯·明斯(Chris Minns)周六表示：“我们希望这些枪支被上交、赔偿并安全销毁。” 国家已经推行的枪支所有权改革意味着个人只能拥有四支枪支——尽管有些人，例如农民和体育射击运动员，最多可以拥有 10 支枪支。 该计划将提供给那些拥有比新规则允许的武器数量更多的人，或者不再受许可证保护的人——期限从五年减少到两年。 该计划将分两个阶段实施。第一个 - 从 11 月初开始 - 涵盖手枪、霰弹枪和步枪的类型。 例如，交出一把左轮手枪的人将获得 1,000 澳元的报酬，而交出一把气步枪的人将获得 450 澳元的报酬。 第二阶段将于明年初开始，涵盖价值 3,000 澳元以上的“高价值枪支”，上限为 10,000 澳元。 国家枪支回购计划由新南威尔士州和联邦政府共同资助。 企业将能够获得高达 25,000 澳元的支持，以帮助他们适应改革，枪支经销商也可以获得帮助。 总理安东尼·阿尔巴内斯表示：“我们必须尽一切努力确保邦迪反犹太主义恐怖袭击不再发生。 去年12月14日，在澳大利亚最著名的海滩附近举行光明节庆祝活动时，包括一名10岁女孩和一名大屠杀幸存者在内的15人被杀。 澳大利亚当局最初计划在全国范围内回购枪支，但该计划因资金和实施方式而被推迟。

title.en: Rescuers search desperately for survivors as Indonesian quake kills dozens of people
title.zh: 印度尼西亚地震造成数十人死亡，救援人员拼命寻找幸存者

summary.en: Rescue teams are scrambling to get to the region closest to the epicentre of an Indonesian earthquake where landslides have blocked roads.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Rescuers have combed through debris for survivors after a powerful earthquake struck off Indonesia's eastern Flores island , killing at least 47 people, according to disaster officials.

The national disaster management agency (BNPB) raised the death toll from 40 late on Saturday, and rescue official Fathur Rahman said 50 people were injured in the 7.7-magnitude quake.

Suharyanto, who leads the BNPB, said earlier that people were trapped in several buildings.

"These will be the initial targets of the disaster response teams," said Suharyanto, who like many Indonesians uses one name.

Nearly 160 houses, dozens of educational and health facilities and other public buildings were damaged when the earthquake struck the popular tourist island in Indonesia's east, the BNPB reported.

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said preparations were underway to bring aid to some 2,000 people in temporary shelters.

The government sent 50,000 aid packages weighing a total of 275 tonnes to the area, and European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen offered help from the bloc's Copernicus Earth observation satellites.

"Europe stands ready to deploy Copernicus, our eyes in the sky, to support search and rescue efforts. Indonesia, we stand with you," she wrote on X.

"I have never felt an earthquake this big," Yulian Juita Ekalia, who lives in Ruteng city more than 100 kilometres west of the epicentre, told AFP by telephone hours after the tremor.

"It felt like we were on a trampoline; it was really scary," said the 37-year-old university lecturer, who was jolted awake at around 5.30am local time on Saturday.

"As I rushed to get outside, everything in the house fell down: the television, my son's trophies, the dish racks, suitcases on top of the wardrobes. When I got outside, my son and neighbours were already there, screaming in fear."

Rescue official Fathur told AFP the focus was on locating victims who may be buried under rubble, but rescue efforts have been complicated by landslides cutting off roads.

Residents in Nagekeo, an area close to the epicentre, raced for higher ground as the sea retreated early Saturday — a possible sign of an approaching tsunami , AFP journalists witnessed.

While a tsunami warning was lifted, authorities urged people not to return to damaged buildings for fear that aftershocks may bring them down.

Hundreds remained outside hours later as dozens of aftershocks shook the island, the strongest measured at a magnitude of 6.1.

Waves of up to 1.6 metres were reported in some coastal regions of Flores, according to Indonesia's BMKG geological agency.

title.en: Qatar denies capturing three Iranian pilots after downing fighter jets
title.zh: 卡塔尔否认在击落战斗机后抓获三名伊朗飞行员

summary.en: Iran claims they have been held since Qatar downed two fighter jets at the start of the US-Iran war.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Iran has called for the release of three Iranian pilots it said were captured by Qatar after two fighter jets were hit by air defences during a military operation at the start of the US-Iran war.

In a letter to the head of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), Iran's Brig Gen Mohammad Bagherzadeh said the pilots - Javad Salehi, Abdul Majid Dashtian, and Imran Behroshian - had been held captive for six months.

He said the body of a fourth pilot, Majid Kazemi, was returned after he was killed in the same operation on 2 March 2026 - the third day of the war.

Qatar "categorically denied" Iran's claims and said it was "surprised by these misleading statements".

Gen Bagherzadeh said the three pilots had been captured by Qatar after they ejected from their jets during the combat mission on a Qatari military base.

In the letter to ICRC chief Mirjana Spoljaric, published by Iranian media, he accused Qatar of violating "the inalienable rights of these prisoners, contrary to all international laws and regulations".

The letter also claimed the three pilots had not been allowed to meet or contact their families.

Qatar's foreign affairs spokesperson Majed Mohammed Al Ansari said contact had been made with the pilots "after they violated Qatari airspace", but it did not receive a response.

"The necessary measures were taken to defend our territory in accordance with international law," he added in a statement on X.

Al Ansari said Qatar's search and rescue teams "carried out their duties to the fullest extent in searching for the pilots' remains".

He said Qatar contacted Iran to "co-ordinate the handover of the remains of one of the pilots that were recovered", and that Tehran had yet to respond to an invitation to review details of the search and rescue operation.
body.zh: 伊朗呼吁释放三名伊朗飞行员，据称是在美伊战争开始时的一次军事行动中两架战斗机被防空系统击中后被卡塔尔俘虏的。 伊朗准将穆罕默德·巴格尔扎德在致红十字国际委员会主席的一封信中表示，这三名飞行员——贾瓦德·萨利希、阿卜杜勒·马吉德·达什蒂安和伊姆兰·贝罗希安——已被关押了六个月。 他说，第四名飞行员马吉德·卡泽米 (Majid Kazemi) 的尸体于 2026 年 3 月 2 日（即战争的第三天）在同一行动中丧生后被归还。 卡塔尔“断然否认”伊朗的说法，并表示“对这些误导性言论感到惊讶”。 巴格扎德将军表示，这三名飞行员在卡塔尔军事基地执行战斗任务时从飞机上弹射，随后被卡塔尔抓获。 在伊朗媒体发表的致红十字国际委员会主席米里亚娜·斯波尔贾里奇的信中，他指责卡塔尔侵犯了“这些囚犯不可剥夺的权利，违反了所有国际法律和法规”。 信中还声称，三名飞行员不被允许会见或联系他们的家人。 卡塔尔外交事务发言人马吉德·穆罕默德·安萨里表示，“在飞行员侵犯卡塔尔领空后”与他们进行了联系，但没有收到回应。 “我们根据国际法采取了必要措施来保卫我们的领土，”他在 X 的一份声明中补充道。 安萨里表示，卡塔尔搜救队“在搜寻飞行员遗体方面尽了最大努力”。 他说，卡塔尔已联系伊朗，“协调已找到的一名飞行员遗体的移交”，而德黑兰尚未回应审查搜救行动细节的邀请。

title.en: Morocco detains dozens of migrants trying to cross into Ceuta, reports say
title.zh: 据报道，摩洛哥拘留数十名试图越境进入休达的移民

summary.en: Moroccan authorities have reportedly detained dozens of migrants attempting to cross into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta. Security measures were heightened following social media suggestions of another large-scale crossing attempt.
summary.zh: 据报道，摩洛哥当局拘留了数十名试图越境进入西班牙飞地休达的移民。社交媒体上出现关于周六可能发生第二次大规模越境的传言后，安全措施已加强。

body.en:
Moroccan authorities have intercepted dozens of migrants seeking to cross into the Spanish North African exclave of Ceuta, reports say.

More than 100 people were blocked trying to make their way to the border on the outskirts of the town of Fnideq, according to Moroccan security sources cited by Spanish media and the Reuters news agency.

It comes a fortnight after roughly 78,000 migrants arrived in the exclave by sea in a matter of hours - 100 of whom died, according to the city's mayor, who also said the vast majority of arrivals had returned to Morocco.

Security had been stepped up in the area after the influx and amid suggestions on social media of a second mass crossing attempt this weekend.

The security sources said 111 people had been detained in or around Fnideq - known in Spanish as Castillejos - about 3km (1.8 miles) from the border, the majority of whom were from sub-Saharan Africa.

Moroccan police - including some in riot gear - reportedly used tear gas to disperse groups of migrants gathered on nearby hills.

Earlier this week, Morocco's government said it was monitoring "the circulation of social media posts and messages of unknown origin" calling for a mass crossing on Saturday, and warned that it would prosecute organisers and participants.

Security at the breakwater entrance was "10 times stronger than the previous day", Spanish newspaper El País reported.

Morocco had dispatched army officers, navy speedboats and drones to the border on Saturday, it said.

Spain has also installed a metal fence and a floating barrier following last month's influx.

The crisis had calmed since breaking out in late July, but it has sparked tensions between EU nations which share open borders as well as criticism of the Spanish government.

Italy suspended the 29-member Schengen arrangement of free movement with Spain and introduced border checks on arrivals from Spain.

Italy was backed by Finland and Denmark, while the Czech Republic called for Spain's membership to be temporarily suspended.

Spain reacted angrily, with Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez noting Ceuta was not part of the Schengen area - and the migrants, therefore, had not arrived on the Spanish mainland and could travel to any other European country.

It urged Italy to drop its border controls - and introduced its own when Rome refused, citing the possibility of a new influx on 15 August.

On Saturday, Italy's Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said his country had been afraid of a "risk of a new wave of arrivals in Ceuta".

"We're not waging any kind of 'battle' against Spain; we're simply carefully controlling arrivals," he said.

"Instead of worrying about us, Spain should worry about Morocco: that's where the problems are coming from, certainly not from our controls."

When Fujisawa walked out of prison for the fifteenth time, he had nowhere to go. No home, and no family waiting for him. After spending a total of 35 years behind bars for repeated shoplifting, remaining free meant uncertainty.

Fujisawa had been stealing tiny items of little use to him—lipstick, food, whatever he could grab quickly. Despite severe sentencing for repeat offenders in Japan, prison was never much of a deterrent. It meant returning to a community he was comfortable in.

"Once you’re in, you’re among friends, people who will accept who you are, whatever your background," he says.

Now in his seventies, Fujisawa has spent much of his adult life moving between prison and the outside world.

"I kept going in and out of prison," he says. I was only out in society for one or two years at a time."

While Fujisawa's story is extreme, he is part of a much broader problem in Japan.

Japan has one of the world's oldest populations, with more than a quarter of its citizens aged 65 or older. Its offenders are ageing too.

The proportion of elderly offenders has climbed despite overall crime rates falling dramatically. With people over 60 making up of more than a quarter of arrests in some parts of the country, many are accused of petty theft.

Volunteer probation officer Chiba has observed this shift. He says 20 to 30 per cent of his parolees are elderly.

"Being isolated and the rising cost of living, some old people don't receive enough pension. They run short on money, so they repeat crimes."

According to government data, around half of elderly people caught shoplifting live by themselves, with four in 10 saying they have no family or rarely speak to them.

The number of Japanese seniors living alone has dramatically increased over recent decades, leaving many to face old age with little financial or social support.

Elderly offenders also have some of Japan's highest rates of reoffending. Nearly one in five prisoners over 60 returns to prison within two years of being released.

Last year, the government amended the Penal Code, abolishing mandatory prison labour and introducing rehabilitation programs to give prisoners skills to help them cope with life on the outside.

But former prisoners coming back to the outside still face social stigma. Many struggle to find work and secure housing.

"Historically in Japan, our attitudes towards former prisoners and how we treat them has not been good," Chiba says .

title.en: The surprising story behind Fiji's deep ties to Israel
title.zh: 斐济与以色列深厚渊源背后的惊人故事

summary.en: Fiji's unexpected and strong relationship with Israel is rooted in a unique national origin story that has influenced both the island nation's local faith practices and its international diplomatic approach.
summary.zh: 斐济与以色列之间出人意料的紧密关系，植根于一个独特的国家起源故事，这个故事影响了斐济的乡村信仰实践及其国际外交政策。

body.en:
Share your feedback and help us improve this feature. Read more about how we use AI at SBS here.

Long ago, the story goes, a great double-hulled canoe called the Kaunitoni came from the west, carrying the first ancestral chiefs of the iTaukei (indigenous Fijians). At its head, in one version of the tradition, stood their leader, Lutunasobasoba.

The voyagers had come a seemingly impossible distance: from Thebes in ancient Egypt — earlier still, some say, from a place farther west, via Israel — down the Nile to Lake Tanganyika, across the Indian Ocean, and finally to Vuda, on the western coast of Viti Levu, Fiji's largest island.

In some tellings, it carried the written record of the people's laws and genealogies — lost, like the canoe's other cargo, somewhere in the churning sea.

For most of the past century, this has been one of the best-known versions of Fiji's national origin story. The mission schools taught it; so did the primary schools. Radio carried it further still, until it became part of the way generations of Fijians understood their ancestry.

Only, much of it was invented in the 1890s — set down for the first time in a newspaper.

The colonial government's Fijian-language paper, Na Mata, ran a competition at the time, inviting readers across the archipelago to send in the definitive account of where the Fijian people had come from, with the best to be printed.

The winning entry ran over 17 instalments, centring on a forgotten tribe. Within a few decades it had acquired the weight of history.

Behind the claimed migration sits a larger conviction, still widely held in some iTaukei communities and church groups: that Fijians descend from a Lost Tribe of Israel — one of 10 the Hebrew Bible describes as carried into exile and never heard from again.

The belief has no support in mainstream science or archaeology. Yet it has helped foster a distinctive affinity with Israel.

The particulars shift from place to place. On Mana Island, in the Yasawa group off western Viti Levu, the Ark of the Covenant — the gold-covered chest that, in the Book of Exodus, held the Ten Commandments — is said to lie buried.

In a village in Ba, in Viti Levu's north-west, an elder once pointed to a rock and told Reverend Marika Baleidelabaci, a Fijian historian and Methodist minister, that Jesus had been born exactly there.

In the Navosa highlands, markings cut into a cave wall are read by some as ancient Hebrew — an interpretation, Baleidelabaci says, that came back with Fijian soldiers who had served in the Middle East and recognised the shapes.

summary.en: Twenty-two more bodies have been recovered after a boat accident on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe, bringing the death toll to 68. Among those killed were 18 children, following the ferry's capsizing on Tuesday.

body.en:
Twenty-two more bodies have been recovered after a boat accident in Zimbabwe , taking the death toll to 68, police said on Saturday.

The ferry capsized on Tuesday on Lake Kariba , on the border with Zambia. An investigation has suggested it was overloaded when it turned over during heavy winds.

Eighteen children were among the people killed, Zimbabwe’s police said, in what is believed to be the country’s deadliest such disaster.

Most of the passengers are believed to be villagers and fish traders who lived around the lake.

Officials said the vessel was authorised to carry 90 people but was packed with 114 adults, five crew members and an unspecified number of children.

Lt Col Joseph Muchechesi, commander of the boat regiment involved in the search operation, said: “So far today we have managed to take 22 bodies. We are confident that we will manage to retrieve all the bodies.”

Hundreds of people gathered at the district hospital in the lakeside town of Kariba to identify the bodies of their relatives and loved ones.

A public memorial service was held in Kariba, nearly 280km (175 miles) north-west of the capital Harare, on Thursday before the burials started.

Survivors said they pleaded with the ferry driver to turn back as the vessel had begun taking on water soon after departing.

Chance Siyamavhu, 45, told Agence France-Presse: “Thank God that a wave pushed the sinking vessel and we managed to climb on top.

“When the boat capsized, most of the people scrambled to get the lifejackets but most of them did not even know how to use them.

Lake Kariba is the world’s largest manmade lake by volume. It stretches more than 200km (124 miles) and is up to 40km (25 miles) wide in places.

It was created in the 1950s during British colonial rule, when the Zambezi River was dammed, displacing about 57,000 people.

In 2014, 26 people, 24 of them children, drowned in Zambia’s part of the lake, when the boat meant to transport them to independence day celebrations capsized.

Thousands of Bonnie Tyler fans lined the streets of her home town in south Wales to pay respects to the singer as her coffin was brought back to her former home.

The singer, whose real name was Gaynor Sullivan, died unexpectedly on 8 July in Portugal at the age of 75.

Many fans stood along Newton Road in Mumbles, Swansea , to watch the procession as her coffin was brought back. The coffin was draped in the Welsh flag and accompanied by a framed photograph of the singer.

Fans threw flowers on to the hearse, and the crowd erupted into applause and broke out into a rendition of Total Eclipse of the Heart.

Mumbles was Tyler’s part-time home, as she split her time between Algarve in Portugal and a large Victorian house in Blackpill, near Mumbles, overlooking Swansea Bay.

Tyler became renowned globally for her pop music hits, including Total Eclipse of the Heart and I Need a Hero.

Among those waiting to pay their respects to Tyler was Carys Edwards, 18, who said the singer was “an inspiration to everybody”.

She told PA Media: “Her music touched a lot of people, especially me. I’m quite surprised how many people came here today, but then not as well, because she was such an icon.

“She was always coming home and making sure that she came back to her fans in Wales .

“Her songs really did touch a lot of people here in Wales, we loved her a lot. When we found out she passed away, it was such a heartbreak to all of us. We cried and everything.”

Michael Bone, 58, and his partner Alan Hawkins, 54, travelled from Derby to watch the procession.

“We thought it’d be nice to pay our respects,” said Bone. “For me personally, it’s because in my teens, her music was quite prolific. For me, it was her most iconic period in the 1980s.”

Others were reported to have travelled from as far as Austria to witness the procession of Tyler’s coffin.

Her other hits included It’s a Heartache and If You Were a Woman (And I Was a Man). She represented the UK in the 2013 Eurovision song contest in Malmö, Sweden, with the song Believe in Me, finishing in 19th place.

A celebration of Tyler’s life is set to take place at Swansea Minster (Church of St Mary’s) on Monday 17 August. Only those with invitations will be allowed inside, but the service will be shown on a large screen in nearby St David’s Square – and members of the public can pay their respects.

After the service, Tyler’s coffin will make a final journey through her home village of Skewen – followed by a private gathering strictly for family and friends.

summary.en: Lebanon's prime minister denounced the attacks on villages in southern Lebanon for targeting civilians in their homes. Israel said it was firing on Hezbollah infrastructure.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Lebanon's prime minister denounced the attacks on villages in southern Lebanon for targeting civilians in their homes. Israel said it was firing on Hezbollah infrastructure.

At least 11 people were killed when Israel launched fresh airstrikes in southern Lebanon  on Saturday, the deadliest since the Israel-Hezbollah truce nearly two months ago.

The attacks were met with defiance by the Iran-backed Hezbollah , which demanded an end to "humiliating" peace negotiations with Israel .

The Lebanese Health Ministry said one of the strikes, on the edge of the village of Ansar, killed seven people and wounded two.

The strike, which happened at dawn, hit a house and destroyed it, according to NNA, the Lebanese state news agency.

Germany's DPA news agency cited residents as saying the property served as a base for Hezbollah.

The second strike hit the village of Deir al-Zahrani, killing four and wounding 17.

NNA reported other strikes around the strategic Ali Taher hill, which overlooks parts of the southern city of Nabatiyeh and key roads to it.

The Israeli military confirmed hitting Hezbollah infrastructure in southern Lebanon, saying it was retaliation for an attack by the militia on Israeli forces.

Later Saturday, Hezbollah hit back at the latest strikes, saying they would be met with an "appropriate" response.

Israel "must clearly understand that its attacks, violations and attempts to impose a fait accompli cannot continue, and will be met with an appropriate response", the Iran-backed group said in a statement.

Hezbollah warned Lebanese authorities against continuing its "humiliating" negotiations with Israel, which would provide "the enemy with free concessions."

Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam denounced the strikes, calling on Israel to "halt this escalation."

"The seven martyrs of the Israeli airstrike on the town of Ansar are not military infrastructure and the children and women killed were not military targets,” he wrote on X.

The Israel–Hezbollah war reignited in early March around the start of the  Iran war , when Hezbollah launched attacks on northern Israel to avenge the killing of Iran’s Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

It rapidly became a full-scale conflict that involved Israeli ground operations in southern Lebanon, mass evacuations of residents and the deaths of over 4,300 people.

Israel claims to have established the so-called security zone in southern Lebanon to prevent Hezbollah attacks on northern Israel.

title.en: Russians snap up new homes built on Ukraine 'graveyard'

summary.en: Russia is constructing high-rises in the occupied Ukrainian city of Mariupol, on the sites of buildings it destroyed. Who's buying these properties? And what happened to the Ukrainians who used to lived here?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Russia is constructing high-rises in the occupied Ukrainian city of Mariupol, on the sites of buildings it destroyed. Who's buying these properties? And what happened to the Ukrainians who used to lived here?

Halyna Artemova, an English teacher, lived in Mariupol for almost 40 years, at Metallurgy Avenue 87.

"It's my beloved city. When I look at the photos, it brings tears to my eyes. I know every crack in the asphalt, every tree," she told DW. Her apartment block in the city on the Sea of Azov was struck by a missile during a Russian attack in March 2022.

Photographer Yevhen Sosnovsky and his wife lived in the house next door, Metallurgy Avenue 85, for 20 years. "I did everything myself, all the interior renovations, and the furniture," he said. "We invested a lot in it; we planned to spend our twilight years there, living quietly." His building also caught fire during the missile attack, and residents were driven out by Russian troops. They weren't even allowed to take food or clothing with them.

Now there's a parking lot where Sosnovsky's apartment block used to be. Next door, where Artemova once lived, stands a new building. The Russian building contractor Su-2007, which operates in the Ukrainian regions occupied by Russia, cleared several buildings on Metallurgy Avenue that were destroyed in the war and constructed high-rise apartment blocks in their place. These form part of a residential complex now known as the Leningradsky Kvartal.

"They're building on human bones, and fast, to eradicate the traces of their crimes," said Sosnovsky.

DW is not allowed in to the Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine, so cannot report directly from city. However, it is possible to get an idea of what life is like in Mariupol today by talking to people who used to live there, studying satellite images, and doing research online.

Many people who have moved into the new apartments on Metallurgy Avenue communicate with each other online in neighborhood forums. From these forums, it's clear that the majority bought the apartments either to live in themselves, or to rent out.

In chats, they ask how they can get furniture delivered from Russia, or which kindergarten or school they should choose for their children. People are reminded that the most important thing when submitting documents is that they should be of Russian origin.

Not everyone has finished remodeling their apartments, and some people with small children take the opportunity to complain: "It's too late! Stop the goddamn renovations! Or maybe you're pro-Ukrainian and oppose Russian laws?"

Economist Vyacheslav Shiryaev said apartments in the new buildings in Mariupol are being bought primarily by incomers: Russian security personnel, officials and people working in military...
body.zh: 俄罗斯正在被占领的乌克兰城市马里乌波尔的废墟上建造高层建筑。谁在购买这些房产？曾经住在这里的乌克兰人怎么样了？ Halyna Artemova 是一名英语教师，她在马里乌波尔冶金大道 87 号居住了近 40 年。 “这是我深爱的城市。当我看到这些照片时，我热泪盈眶。我知道沥青路上的每一条裂缝，每一棵树，”她告诉德国之声。她位于亚速海城市的公寓楼在 2022 年 3 月的俄罗斯袭击中被导弹击中。 摄影师叶夫亨·索斯诺夫斯基 (Yevhen Sosnovsky) 和他的妻子在隔壁冶金大道 85 号的房子里住了 20 年。 “所有的事情都是我自己做的，所有的室内装修和家具，”他说。 “我们投入了很多，打算在那里安度晚年，安静地生活。”他的大楼也在导弹袭击中起火，居民被俄罗斯军队赶出。他们甚至不被允许携带食物或衣服。 现在索斯诺夫斯基的公寓楼原来是一个停车场。隔壁是阿尔特莫娃曾经居住过的地方，矗立着一座新建筑。在被俄罗斯占领的乌克兰地区开展业务的俄罗斯建筑承包商Su-2007清除了冶金大道上几座在战争中被摧毁的建筑物，并在其所在地建造了高层公寓楼。这些是现在称为列宁格勒克瓦塔尔的住宅区的一部分。 索斯诺夫斯基说：“他们正在人骨上快速建造，以消除他们的犯罪痕迹。” 德国之声不允许进入俄罗斯占领的乌克兰地区，因此无法直接从城市报道。然而，通过与曾经住在那里的人交谈、研究卫星图像和在线研究，可以了解马里乌波尔今天的生活。 许多搬进冶金大道新公寓的人都在社区论坛上在线交流。从这些论坛可以明显看出，大多数人购买公寓要么是为了自己居住，要么是为了出租。 在聊天中，他们询问如何从俄罗斯获得家具，或者应该为孩子选择哪家幼儿园或学校。 人们被提醒，提交文件时最重要的是它们应该是俄罗斯裔。 并不是每个人都完成了他们的公寓的改造，一些带着小孩的人趁机抱怨：“太晚了！停止该死的装修！或者也许你是亲乌克兰的，反对俄罗斯法律的？” 经济学家维亚切斯拉夫·希里亚耶夫 (Vyacheslav Shiryaev) 表示，马里乌波尔新建筑中的公寓主要由外来者购买：俄罗斯安全人员、官员和军队工作人员……

body.en:
While ongoing military actions in Gaza and settler attacks on Palestinians in the occupied West Bank have largely isolated Israel globally, Latin America's authoritarian right sees an opening for a strategic alliance.

A three-week military offensive in the Gaza Strip  in 2009, which killed more than 1,400 people, including an estimated 1,100 civilians, spurred Venezuela's Socialist president at the time, Hugo Chavez, to expel the Israeli ambassador in protest and end diplomatic relations.

Seventeen years later, Venezuela and Israel have agreed to establish a mechanism for the resumption of consular services. It's a limited step, but one that until recently would have been unthinkable.

In Colombia , the nationalist government of new President Abelardo de la Espriella recently reversed the decision by his predecessor, Gustavo Petro , to sever diplomatic relations with Israel in protest of the country's most recent war in Gaza , which has killed more than 70,000 people, nearly one-third of them children.

De la Espriella has even announced that Colombia will relocate its embassy to Jerusalem, and this week declared that Colombia would join the United States as the only two countries that recognize "Israeli sovereignty" over the Golan Heights, which is Syrian territory under international law but has been occupied by Israel since 1967. The vast majority of the international community, including Germany and the UN, does not recognize the annexation of the Golan Heights by Israel.

"There is a trend toward rapprochement with Israel as a response to the surge of the radical right in the region," said Isaac Caro, a professor at Alberto Hurtado University in Chile. Caro said authoritarians in Latin America were linking relations with Israel to "an active alignment with US foreign policy ." He said reinforcing ties with Israel had become a characteristic of Latin America's radical right as part of the renewed discourse of region's place in Judeo-Christian Western civilization.

In Argentina, for example, ultraconservative President Javier Milei has made close relations with Israel a defining feature of both his foreign policy and his own political identity.

Daniel Wajner, associate professor of international relations at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, said there had been a "surge" in diplomacy between Israel and Latin American governments. Wajner said Jair Bolsonaro , the neoliberal former president of Brazil, and El Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele, the self-described "world's coolest dictator," were early adopters of warmer ties with Israel. They were followed by Milei and others.

Transit through the Strait of Hormuz appears to have ground to a near ‌standstill after two more ships were attacked and the United States said it could maintain a naval blockade of Iran indefinitely.

A senior Iranian source said there had been no progress in talks to build on ‌a June agreement to end the war.

Since the ceasefire renewed in the June deal broke down, Iran has resumed attacks on ships it accuses of trying to transit the strait without its permission.

The United Arab Emirates' Abu Dhabi National Oil ‌Company said two of its vessels were attacked transiting the strait on Thursday evening. The UAE government blamed Iran, which made no immediate comment.

Two vessels passed through the narrow waterway on Friday, according to analysis from ship tracking firm Kpler: a grain ship entering Iranian waters and an empty dry bulk ship going in the other direction.

A separate empty liquefied petroleum products tanker was sailing into the Gulf via the strait, the data showed. There were no crude oil shipments visible on Friday.

Some ships may pass through undetected with their transponders off, but the figures are nowhere near the more than 130 ‌ships that traversed the Strait ‌of Hormuz daily before the war launched ⁠by the US and Israel on Iran in February.

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth told reporters the US military has the capability to maintain a naval presence in the region to enforce its retaliatory blockade of Iran, which has inflicted severe economic damage on the country.

"Indefinitely, the United States Navy can maintain a blockade like that because we'll rotate ships in and out, as we have, and we'll continue to," he told reporters during a trip to Panama.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US planned to inflict more financial damage on Iran.

"Watch this space for more announcements coming next week because we are ⁠going to apply measures like have never been seen in the history of economic isolation on a country," he said in an ‌interview on Newsmax.

US President Donald Trump is under pressure at home to end an unpopular war, with high fuel prices dragging down his approval ratings and potentially eroding his party's control of Congress in midterm elections in November.

title.zh: 印度尼西亚强震死亡人数升至38人

summary.en: A powerful earthquake in Indonesia has resulted in at least 38 fatalities, with initial concerns about a potential tsunami.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚发生强烈地震，造成至少38人死亡，此前一度引发了对破坏性海啸的担忧。

body.en:
At least 38 people have died after a 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck eastern Indonesia on Saturday, which was followed by dozens of aftershocks.

"Thirty-eight people have been confirmed dead, two were seriously injured, 11 sustained minor injuries, and approximately 2,000 people have evacuated on their own," Indonesian National Disaster Mitigation Agency chief Suharyanto told a news conference on Saturday.

The earthquake struck off Flores island in eastern Indonesia early Saturday, sending thousands running in panic after authorities issued a tsunami warning.

Tsunami waves of less than one metre were recorded in several areas of the Southeast Asian nation. The warning was later lifted.

Residents in Nagekeo regency on Flores, the area closest to the epicentre, raced for higher ground as the sea retreated.

Teams had yet to reach Nagekeo, and communications signals there had been ‌affected, Fathur Rahman, head of the city's rescue agency, told Reuters.

Attempts to reach Nagekeo ⁠by car were blocked by landslides, while another team was attempting to go by ferry, he said.

About 2,000 residents in Nagekeo evacuated, and damage was reported to a number of houses, warehouses and government facilities, national disaster mitigation agency BNPB said.

Authorities also reported traffic congestion and power outages affecting parts of the regency, it said.

The governor of East Nusa Tenggara Province, Emanuel Melkiades Laka Lena, told a media conference at least five people died from collapsing rubble as they slept.

The epicentre of the shallow quake was located off the north coast of the island, about 68 kilometres northwest of the coastal town of Ende, US and Indonesian authorities said.

The initial jolt was followed by strong aftershocks in the same area, including one with a magnitude of 6.1.

"Suddenly it started to shake and I panicked," 31-year-old hospital customer service official and Maumere resident, Lukas Lotar, told AFP.

"Patients also fled the hospital, the jolt was big. I saw some walls were cracked," he said.

A resident in Nagekeo, Yohanes Babo, 56, said he was at a market when the earth started shaking.

"The shaking was strong. Thankfully, we were already outside the house," he told AFP.

"People were panicking, running here and there. We're evacuating for the time being... and trying to get to the hills," he said, adding: "My family is safe. No one was harmed."

Strong shaking was also felt across East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara and parts of South Sulawesi, and residents in several areas reported shaking lasting about one minute, BNPB said in a statement.

title.en: Donald Trump to declare Hormuz US territory 'soon'
title.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普“很快”宣布霍尔木兹为美国领土

summary.en: Donald Trump said the strait would become part of the US after Iran is defeated. He also told Americans to accept higher gas prices, which have soared since Iran closed Hormuz in response to US and Israeli attacks.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Donald Trump said the strait would become part of the US after Iran is defeated. He also told Americans to accept higher gas prices, which have soared since Iran closed Hormuz in response to US and Israeli attacks.

President Donald Trump said Friday that he would "soon" declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory.

"After we finish defeating Iran , which is being very badly defeated — pretty soon I'll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States," Trump said at a rally at a police academy in Garden City, New York state. "It's true," he added.

It was not clear whether his remarks were serious or whether they signal a new policy shift for Washington in its war against Tehran , which is more than five months old.

Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi dismissed Trump's remarks, saying the country would "not be intimidated" and that the strategic waterway would remain under its control and authority.

The US and Israel launched the war against Iran on February 28. At the time, senior White House officials, including Trump, said the aim was to end Iran's nuclear program and spark a popular uprising to force regime change in the Islamic Republic, among other goals.

Iran's response has been to target US allies across the Middle East with drone and missile strikes, as well as to impose a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, through which one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) shipments passed before the war.

The US responded to Iran's closure of the strait with its own naval blockade of Iranian ships and ports. The two countries have been locked in a stalemate over the vital waterway for months, causing energy prices to soar.

Rising oil and gas costs and the economic fallout from the war are likely to be leading issues in the midterm elections in November.

During the rally, the US president also urged Americans to accept that they would have to "pay a tiny little bit more" for their gasoline as a worthy price for preventing "a very evil country" from getting a nuclear weapon.

"What we're doing is a great service for the world, not only for ourselves ... and we're really doing a ​great job," Trump told the crowd, adding that "no ships get through (the US blockade of Hormuz) unless we want them to."

On Friday, Trump also dismissed concerns over the living conditions aboard a US aircraft carrier that was deployed to the Middle East amid the war with Iran.

Relatives of service members aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln told US military media outlets that personnel are struggling with difficult living conditions and deteriorating mental health . There have also been reports of suicide attempts.

body.en: Despite the recent hearings in Congress, we seem to be even further from the goal of understanding Covid-19’s origin’s than we have ever been As a microbiologist and infectious disease clinician, it has been tough to watch the recent devolution of public discourse on Covid-19 origins. It has been especially difficult for me to read the comments of Anthony Fauci about the origins debate in his now-public diary . And it has been painful to watch the televised spectacle hosted by the US senator Rand Paul on 29 July involving a hostile interrogation of Fauci. Despite many early pleas, including my own , for a dispassionate, objective assessment of what we know, don’t know and need to know about Covid-19 origins, we seem to be even further from this goal now than we have ever been – plagued by politicization, polarization and illogical thinking. summary.en: Jennifer Hubbard and other letter writers express concern that Western nations are ignoring China's repressive regime, particularly its 'ethnic unity' law used to suppress minorities. They argue that meaningful international diplomacy is urgently needed to address these human rights issues.
summary.zh: 詹妮弗·哈伯德及其他来信者表示，西方国家对中国压制性政权，特别是其用于压制少数民族的“民族团结”法视而不见。他们认为，急需有意义的国际外交来解决这些人权问题。

body.en: Meaningful diplomacy on an international level is well overdue, writes Jennifer Hubbard . Plus letters from Geoffrey Dixon and Jane Renton In his article on China’s latest tool for suppression of minorities, the “ethnic unity” law, Simon Tisdall seems to take it as read that western governments will continue to pay lip service to notions of human rights in China while pursuing short-term economic goals, ultimately destructive to their own productivity ( President Xi never wastes a good crisis. As Iran, Ukraine and Palestine distract the world, he tightens his grip, 8 August ). This has been the pattern since June 1989, the Tiananmen Square massacre. His faint hope that the young urban Chinese might overturn Xi’s regime is a judgment on the failure of western governments to show any foresight, integrity, effective diplomacy, joined-up thinking or action. They rely on the self-sacrifice of individuals such as Jimmy Lai , Lobga Rangzen and countless – often to us nameless – individuals who put their lives on the line while we wring our hands and weep crocodile tears. Continue reading...
body.zh: 詹妮弗·哈伯德写道，早就应该在国际层面开展有意义的外交。再加上杰弗里·迪克森和简·伦顿的来信。西蒙·蒂斯达尔在其关于中国镇压少数民族的最新工具“民族团结”法的文章中似乎认为，西方政府将继续对中国的人权观念口头上说好，同时追求短期经济目标，最终损害他们自己的生产力（习主席从来不会浪费一场好的危机。随着伊朗、乌克兰和巴勒斯坦分散了世界的注意力，他加强了控制，8月8日）。这就是1989年6月天安门广场屠杀以来的模式。他对中国城市年轻人可能推翻习近平政权的微弱希望是对西方政府未能表现出任何远见、正直、有效外交、联合思维或行动的判断。他们依赖于黎智英（Jimmy Lai）、洛布加·让赞（Lobga Rangzen）等个人的自我牺牲，以及无数（通常对我们来说无名）个人的自我牺牲，他们冒着生命危险，而我们则绞尽脑汁，流下鳄鱼的眼泪。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The call for international diplomacy to address the suppression of minorities echoes the biblical mandate to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves. In a world where powerful voices can overshadow the vulnerable, Yahweh reminds us of our responsibility to advocate for justice and the rights of the destitute. May we seek wisdom and courage to uphold...
reflection.zh: 呼吁国际外交以解决少数民族受压迫的问题，与圣经中为不能为自己说话之人发声的命令不谋而合。在一个强大声音可能掩盖弱势群体的世界里，雅伟提醒我们有责任倡导正义和维护贫困者的权利。愿我们寻求智慧和勇气，维护所有人的尊严，特别是那些声音被压制的人。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Taiwan says it was hit by ‘abnormal’ AI-assisted cyber-attack
title.zh: 台湾称遭受“异常”人工智能辅助网络攻击

summary.en: Taiwan reported detecting "abnormal" AI-assisted cyber-attacks on government agencies last month, originating from overseas. These attacks represent a new kind of threat, with suspected links to China-based hackers.
summary.zh: 台湾报告称，上个月侦测到来自海外、由人工智能辅助的“异常”网络攻击，目标是政府机构。这些攻击代表了一种新型威胁，据称与中国相关黑客有关。

body.en: Taiwan’s statement comes a day after reports that suspected China-linked hackers had carried out a first-of-a-kind breach Taiwan says it detected AI-assisted cyber-attacks on government agencies that came from overseas last month, a new kind of threat that has been reported as “first-of-a-kind breach”. The Ministry of Digital Affairs (MDA) said its cybersecurity monitoring units ‌detected the “abnormal attack” targeting government agencies, which began on 20 July. The National Institute of Cyber Security issued a series of warning alerts while it investigated. Continue reading...
body.zh: 台湾发表声明的前一天，有报道称疑似与中国有关的黑客实施了史无前例的违规行为。台湾表示，上个月检测到来自海外的针对政府机构的人工智能辅助网络攻击，这是一种新的威胁，被报道为“史无前例的违规行为”。数字事务部 (MDA) 表示，其网络安全监控单位检测到 7 月 20 日开始的针对政府机构的“异常攻击”。美国国家网络安全研究所在调查过程中发布了一系列警告。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The emergence of AI-assisted cyber-attacks highlights the constant need for vigilance in a rapidly changing world. Proverbs 27:12 reminds us that wisdom lies in foreseeing danger and taking appropriate refuge. As technology evolves, so must our discernment and protective measures, trusting Yahweh for guidance.
reflection.zh: 人工智能辅助的网络攻击的出现，凸显了在快速变化的世界中保持警惕的持续必要性。箴言27:12提醒我们，智慧在于预见危险并采取适当的避难措施。随着科技发展，我们的洞察力和保护措施也必须随之进步，信靠雅伟的指引。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: With Hollywood struggling in China, can the Odyssey draw a crowd?
title.zh: 好莱坞在中国市场举步维艰，《奥德赛》能否吸引观众？

summary.en: Christopher Nolan's summer blockbuster, "The Odyssey" (likely Oppenheimer), is set for release across China's Imax screens. This comes at a time when Western films generally face difficulties in the Chinese market, and the film itself has reportedly overcome significant opposition.
summary.zh: 克里斯托弗·诺兰的夏季大片《奥德赛》（很可能是《奥本海默》）将在中国各地的IMAX影院上映。目前西方电影在中国市场普遍举步维艰，而这部影片据报道也克服了来自世界首富的猛烈攻击。

body.en: Christopher Nolan’s epic will be released on Friday across most of the country’s 800 Imax screens, at a time when western films have been struggling The Odyssey, Christopher Nolan’s summer blockbuster juggernaut, has overcome an onslaught of attacks from the world’s richest man and stared down criticism from a classicist who translated the poem , to become one of the year’s most celebrated and highest-grossing films. But this week, the film faces one of its biggest challenges yet. Continue reading...
body.zh: 克里斯托弗·诺兰的这部史诗巨制将于周五在全国 800 块 Imax 银幕上上映，当时西方电影一直在苦苦挣扎，克里斯托弗·诺兰的夏季大片《奥德赛》克服了来自世界首富的猛烈攻击，也顶住了翻译这首诗的古典学家的批评，成为今年最著名和票房最高的电影之一。但本周，这部电影面临着迄今为止最大的挑战之一。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Launching any major endeavor, like a film in a challenging market, requires immense effort and hope for success. Proverbs 16:3 reminds us to commit our work to Yahweh, trusting that He will establish our plans. Even when facing significant headwinds, we can find peace in knowing that our diligent efforts are seen and can be blessed.
reflection.zh: 在充满挑战的市场中推出一部电影这样的大型项目，需要付出巨大的努力并寄予成功的希望。箴言16:3提醒我们，要将我们的工作交托给雅伟，相信他会成就我们的计划。即使面对重重阻力，我们也能在知道自己的辛勤努力被看见并蒙福时找到平安。

verse.textEn: Commit to Yahweh whatever you do, and he will establish your plans.
verse.textZh: 你所做的，要交托雅伟，你所谋的，就必成立。

title.en: Zhu Rongji obituary
title.zh: 朱镕基讣告

summary.en: Zhu Rongji, the fifth premier of the People’s Republic of China, has passed away at 97. He was widely recognized as an economic reformer who famously declared China 'the factory of the world' and was regarded as one of the country's most effective administrators.
summary.zh: 中华人民共和国第五任总理朱镕基逝世，享年97岁。他被广泛认为是经济改革家，曾宣布中国成为‘世界工厂’，并被视为该国最有效的管理者之一。

body.en: Premier of the People’s Republic of China regarded as an economic reformer who declared that the country had become ‘the factory of the world’ Zhu Rongji, who has died aged 97, was the fifth premier of the People’s Republic of China and one of its most effective administrators and economic reformers following its foundation in 1949. In 1991, Zhu was summoned to Beijing, in the footsteps of the then president and party secretary Jiang Zemin , and in the aftermath of the 1989 uprisings in Beijing and the collapse of the Soviet Union. Continue reading...
body.zh: 中华人民共和国总理被誉为经济改革家，宣称中国已成为“世界工厂”。 朱镕基去世，享年 97 岁。朱镕基是中华人民共和国第五任总理，也是自 1949 年建国以来最有效的管理者和经济改革家之一。1991 年，朱镕基追随时任国家主席兼党委书记江泽民的脚步，在改革开放之后被召唤到北京。 1989年北京起义和苏联解体。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The passing of a leader like Zhu Rongji marks the end of a significant chapter, reflecting a life dedicated to public service and economic reform. His legacy reminds us that every life is a race run, with efforts and impacts that shape the world around us. Yahweh invites us to consider how we too might finish our own race with integrity and purpose.
reflection.zh: 朱镕基这样一位领导人的逝世，标志着一个重要篇章的结束，反映了他一生致力于公共服务和经济改革。他的遗产提醒我们，每个人的一生都是一场赛跑，其努力和影响塑造着我们周围的世界。雅伟邀请我们思考，我们又将如何以正直和目标跑完自己的赛程。

verse.textEn: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
verse.textZh: 那美好的仗我已经打过了，当跑的路我已经跑尽了，所信的道我已经守住了。

title.en: Mass evacuations in Beijing as Typhoon Dolphin brings more torrential rain to China
title.zh: 台风海豚带来更多暴雨，北京大规模疏散

summary.en: Forecasters warned the Chinese capital could receive more than one-third of its average annual rainfall over 24 hours Thousands of people have been evacuated from areas at risk of flooding and landslides in Beijing, as the remnants of Typhoon Dolphin continue to bring torrential...
summary.zh: 预报员警告称，中国首都北京在24小时内可能迎来超过年平均降雨量三分之一的降水。随着台风“海豚”的残余继续带来暴雨，北京数千人已从有洪水和山体滑坡风险的地区撤离。

body.en: Forecasters warned the Chinese capital could receive more than one-third of its average annual rainfall over 24 hours Thousands of people have been evacuated from areas at risk of flooding and landslides in Beijing, as the remnants of Typhoon Dolphin continue to bring torrential rain to northern and central China. Forecasters warned on Tuesday that the Chinese capital could receive more than 150mm of rain over the following 24 hours, with some districts forecast to exceed 200mm – more than one-third of Beijing’s average annual rainfall of 528mm. Continue reading...
body.zh: 预报员警告说，中国首都24小时内的降雨量可能会达到年平均降雨量的三分之一以上。随着台风“海豚”的余波继续给中国北部和中部地区带来暴雨，北京有数千人已从面临洪水和山体滑坡风险的地区撤离。预报员周二警告说，未来24小时内，中国首都的降雨量可能超过150毫米，部分地区预计将超过200毫米——超过北京年平均降雨量528毫米的三分之一。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As Beijing faces torrential rains and evacuations, the immediate need for safety and shelter is paramount. In times of natural disaster, we are reminded that Yahweh is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Even amidst the chaos, we can find solace and resilience in His unwavering presence.
reflection.zh: 当北京面临暴雨和疏散时，对安全和庇护的即时需求至关重要。在自然灾害面前，我们被提醒雅伟是我们的避难所和力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。即使在混乱之中，我们也能在祂坚定不移的同在中找到慰藉和韧性。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

title.en: Passenger jet billed as China’s answer to Boeing and Airbus prepares to make first international flight
title.zh: 中国C919客机首次国际飞行，欲挑战波音空客主导地位

summary.en: China's domestically produced passenger jet, the Comac C919, is set to undertake its inaugural international flight from Beijing to Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. While this marks a significant step, aviation experts suggest it will take many generations for the aircraft to genuinely challenge the established dominance of...
summary.zh: 中国国产客机C919将执飞从北京到蒙古乌兰巴托的首个国际航班。尽管这标志着一个重要里程碑，但航空专家指出，该机型可能需要几代人的时间才能真正挑战波音和空客等西方制造商在商业航空领域的既有主导地位。

body.en: The Comac C919 will fly from Beijing to Ulaanbaatar in Mongolia, although experts say it could take generations for it to challenge the west’s dominance of the industry China hopes to break into the world of commercial aviation with the first international flight of a Chinese-made passenger jet scheduled for Wednesday. The Comac C919 will take off from Beijing capital international airport at 3pm, landing in Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia, just over two hours later. Continue reading...
body.zh: 中国商飞 C919 将从北京飞往蒙古乌兰巴托，尽管专家表示，它可能需要几代人的时间才能挑战西方在该行业的主导地位。中国希望通过中国制造的客机定于周三进行的首次国际飞行，打入商业航空领域。中国商飞C919飞机将于下午3点从北京首都国际机场起飞，两个多小时后抵达蒙古首都乌兰巴托。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Embarking on a new venture, especially one with global ambitions, requires immense perseverance and a long-term perspective. Just as athletes prepare for a marathon, nations and industries must commit to the arduous journey, understanding that true success often takes generations of sustained effort. This reminds us that significant achievements are built...
reflection.zh: 开启一项新事业，尤其是有全球抱负的事业，需要巨大的毅力和长远的眼光。正如运动员为马拉松做准备一样，国家和行业也必须致力于艰巨的旅程，明白真正的成功往往需要几代人的持续努力。这提醒我们，重大的成就不仅建立在最初的启动上，更建立在坚定不移地跑完这场赛程的持久承诺上，将结果交托给雅伟。

verse.textEn: Therefore, since we are surrounded by such a great cloud of witnesses, let us throw off everything that hinders and the sin that so easily entangles. And let us run with perseverance the race marked out for us.
verse.textZh: 我们既有这许多的见证人，如同云彩围着我们，就当放下各样的重担，脱去容易缠累我们的罪，存心忍耐，奔那摆在我们前头的路程。

title.en: Floods, storms and landslides: Typhoon Dolphin ravages China – in pictures
title.zh: 洪水、风暴和山体滑坡：台风海豚肆虐中国——图片

summary.en: The most powerful tropical cyclone to hit China this year brings strong ⁠winds, torrential rain and flooding to the country’s east coast Typhoon Dolphin hits Beijing as city braces for one-third of annual rainfall over 24 hours Continue reading...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to compassion for vulnerable people. Galatians 6:2 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with practical compassion and welcome, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到对脆弱群体的怜悯。Galatians 6:2提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以具体的怜悯与接纳来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。

title.en: Australia Desk
title.zh: 澳洲栏目

strap.en: Public life, policy, and community stories shaping Australia now.
strap.zh: 关注正在影响澳洲公共生活、政策与社区的新闻。

title.en: Could you save money on your mortgage? As house prices cool and lender rivalry heats up, experts say Australians should ask
title.zh: 你能在抵押贷款上省钱吗？随着房价降温和贷款人竞争加剧，专家表示澳大利亚人应该询问

summary.en: There is talk that lenders are starting to compete more fiercely for customers as demand for new home loans drops Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Homeowners with a mortgage dodged a bullet this week when the Reserve Bank of Australia board chose to...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: There is talk that lenders are starting to compete more fiercely for customers as demand for new home loans drops Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Homeowners with a mortgage dodged a bullet this week when the Reserve Bank of Australia board chose to hold its official cash rate at 4.35%. The reprieve may prove short-lived, though, with a number of economists and financial markets seeing a good chance of another hike this year. Continue reading...
body.zh: 有传言称，随着新住房贷款需求下降，贷款机构开始更加激烈地争夺客户 获取我们的突发新闻电子邮件、免费应用程序或每日新闻播客 本周，澳大利亚储备银行董事会选择将官方现金利率维持在 4.35%，有抵押贷款的房主躲过了一劫。不过，这种缓和可能是短暂的，因为许多经济学家和金融市场认为今年很有可能再次加息。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到和平与克制。Matthew 5:9提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以怜悯、真实与节制来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: Yvonne Whear vanished from a NSW town. Her daughter believes some people aren’t talking
title.zh: 伊冯·惠尔 (Yvonne Whear) 从新南威尔士州的一个小镇消失了。她女儿认为有些人没有说话

summary.en: Police say there is no evidence to suggest the 73-year-old voluntarily disappeared. Gillian Hallac says the family just wants answers Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast The only time Gillian Hallac sees her mother’s face now is on the posters she puts up...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Police say there is no evidence to suggest the 73-year-old voluntarily disappeared. Gillian Hallac says the family just wants answers Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast The only time Gillian Hallac sees her mother’s face now is on the posters she puts up around town. Yvonne Whear can be seen half-smiling on the counters and walls of shops, cafes and supermarkets. But it has been six months since Hallac heard her mother’s voice. “It’s like I was talking to her and then she was gone,” she says. Continue reading...
body.zh: 警方表示，没有证据表明这名 73 岁的老人是自愿失​​踪。吉莉安·哈拉克 (Gillian Hallac) 表示，家人只是想要答案 获取我们的突发新闻电子邮件、免费应用程序或每日新闻播客 现在，吉莉安·哈拉克 (Gillian Hallac) 唯一一次看到她母亲的脸是在她在镇上张贴的海报上。在商店、咖啡馆和超市的柜台和墙壁上都可以看到伊冯·惠尔 (Yvonne Whear) 半微笑的样子。但自从哈拉克听​​到母亲的声音以来，已经过去六个月了。 “就好像我在和她说话，然后她就走了，”她说。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to justice, dignity, and accountability. Micah 6:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with justice tempered by mercy, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到公义、尊严与问责。Micah 6:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以带着怜悯的公义来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: Labor is facing an insurgent One Nation. The path it takes on immigration will define its identity for years to come
title.zh: 工党面临着叛乱的一国党。其移民之路将决定其未来几年的身份

summary.en: Labor has always had a divided soul over immigration. Now it faces a predicament as it looks to hold on to suburban and regional seats Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast The Albanese government places party unity before most other considerations, so it...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Labor has always had a divided soul over immigration. Now it faces a predicament as it looks to hold on to suburban and regional seats Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast The Albanese government places party unity before most other considerations, so it is notable that there is more than one opinion in cabinet about what to do about immigration policy. title.en: Investors have backed off the housing market. But will you benefit?

summary.en: New data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics indicates an 8.6 per cent drop in investor loans during the June quarter, raising questions about the long-term presence of investors in the housing market.

body.en:
Investors are shying away from the housing market — but experts say it might not be the win the government says it is.

New Australian Bureau of Statistics data on loans show investors have pulled back sharply from the housing market in the June quarter.

Treasurer Jim Chalmers said on Friday the lending figures were an "encouraging sign" that Labor's changes to negative gearing and the capital gains discount were working as intended and the market was "shifting in favour of first-home buyers" — even before the changes have officially taken effect.

But experts said the retreat hasn't necessarily translated into the wave of first-home buyers the federal government's property tax changes were designed to generate.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The number of investor loans fell 8.6 per cent in the June quarter, while first-home buyer loans fell a comparatively lower 2.9 per cent, according to ABS data released on Friday.

Independent property researcher Cameron Kusher said ABS' latest lending data was not surprising and reflected a typical knee-jerk reaction to policy changes.

“Across both the number and the value, the biggest falls in lending over the quarter were for investors, which is not really a surprise when you consider the tax changes that have happened,” he said.

The pullback lines up with what major banks have been reporting in their own lending figures, with CBA and NAB both reporting a 15 per cent drop in mortgage applications last quarter, while Westpac saw a 20 per cent drop.

The tax changes were announced in the May budget but aren't set to formally take effect until 1 July 2027. So, this quarter's fall was a reaction to the announcement itself, not the policy in action.

"We may actually see a larger fall when we get to the next quarter, when we see the full impact of a whole quarter of these changes," he said.

Both Kusher and Real Estate Group's economist Luc Redman say investors have not retreated entirely, rather they have changed strategy.

They are still keen on residential property but the type of property they’re chasing has shifted. They are now eyeing properties that have strong rental growth, or yield.

"Early evidence post-budget suggests that investors are enquiring more towards units that tend to have a higher yield and a lower entry point … compared to prior, when investors would be looking at houses that have stronger prospects of capital growth," Redman told SBS News.

Two places, Tasmania and the ACT, didn't see drops in investor interest — which Kusher said could be a sign they're moving toward properties with good rental returns relative to purchase...

title.en: 'Broken and grateful': Alice Springs farewells Kumanjayi Little Baby
title.zh: “心碎又感激”：爱丽斯泉告别库曼贾伊小宝贝

summary.en: There was a sombre atmosphere at Kumanjayi Little Baby's funeral, with speeches punctuated by the cries of mourners.

body.en:
WARNING: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this story includes the name and image of an Indigenous person who has passed away.

Alice Springs is known as the Red Centre of Australia but on 15 August, the community donned pink for the funeral of five-year-old Warlpiri girl, Kumanjayi Little Baby .

Warlpiri Elder and family spokesperson Robin Granites said pink was her favourite colour — it "reminds us of the clothes she used to wear".

"And the times when we would go in the evening, you see the sunset and even the early morning, you see the pink colour of clouds and that ... is a really good colour for us," Granites said ahead of the funeral.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Kumanjayi Little Baby's body was found on 30 April, after she went missing from Old Timers town camp, south of Alice Springs. Her disappearance sparked a five-day search, described as one of the largest search efforts in Northern Territory history.

47-year-old Jefferson Lewis has since been charged with her alleged murder and two other offences that cannot be published for legal reasons .

Pastor Rejeili Paulo-Smith spoke on behalf of Kumanjayi Little Baby's mother at the funeral service.

She requested that her daughter be remembered , "for who she was, not simply for the tragedy of how her life ended".

"Kumanjayi wasn't simply a little girl who was known by the community. She was Mum's baby too. She was a little girl whose presence filled their home and whose absence has left an enormous space," Paulo-Smith said.

It's been almost four months since the death of Kumanjayi Little Baby. During this time, her family and Indigenous communities have engaged in the grieving period and mourning process known as Sorry Business .

In recent months, Paulo-Smith said the community had felt "both broken and grateful".

"Broken because a precious little life has been taken from us far too soon, yet grateful because Kumanjayi Little Baby was here. She was known, she was loved, she mattered," she said.

The week following Kumanjayi Little Baby's death, thousands of Australians gathered at nationwide candlelight vigils.

At a local vigil in Alice Springs, 89-year-old Maya Cifali told NITV News the outpouring of community spirit was unlike anything she had ever seen.

"It is the first time that such a community spirit is felt for all of us," Cifali said.

Granites also believes the local community has displayed the Warlpiri concept of Jintangka; "which means we're all in one, everyone together".

At the funeral, he took the opportunity to thank Australians and people overseas for rallying behind his family during and in the months following the search...

body.en:
Share your feedback and help us improve this feature. Read more about how we use AI at SBS here.

In her backyard, Tamara Scenna takes a deep breath beneath the towering canopy of the Daintree Rainforest in Far North Queensland.

Streams of light filter through layers of ferns and fan palms as she pauses beside a running stream.

Birds sing in an off-beat chorus, providing a tranquil soundtrack to one of the oldest rainforests.

It's the perfect setting for forest bathing — a Japanese practice of immersing oneself in nature.

"I think it's about seeing the forest differently and being able to almost be given permission to slow down and stop and just be," Scenna tells SBS News.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"It took a while to slow down and really have a city adrenaline stop, but after a couple of months we sort of went, 'actually we don't want to go to the city anymore'.

But behind the tranquillity lies a challenge shared by many of the Daintree's roughly 700 residents. Living beyond the electricity grid means finding ways to balance life in this remote rainforest with the realities of modern living.

In 2021, Scenna and her family swapped life in Sydney for the quiet of the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Daintree Rainforest.

Hoping to escape the pace of city life, her family spent a year travelling around Australia before deciding they were ready for a change.

The journey led the couple to settle in the rainforest, with Scenna leaving her public sector job to run a caravan park and restaurant with her husband , Bruno.

But the dream of living among the ancient trees comes with practical challenges. Like many residents in the region, the couple must find their own solutions for powering their home and business.

While the Scennas have a hybrid energy system that includes solar, relying on diesel generators remains a necessity.

They paid about $300,000 for the solar that powers around a third of their business.

Bruno says installing enough solar panels to power their entire operation would be expensive and require clearing more rainforest for additional infrastructure.

"From an environmental perspective, why would you do that when you can have renewable energy? I fundamentally don't understand," he tells SBS News.

Growing uncertainty around fuel costs, including volatility linked to global events , has renewed calls from residents for a renewable energy solution in the Daintree.

title.en: More GPs are asking patients this question. What should you do?
title.zh: 更多全科医生正在问病人这个问题。你该怎么做？

summary.en: General practitioners are increasingly adopting a new practice during patient appointments, which is rapidly spreading. However, this new approach has not been universally accepted, with some expressing reservations.
summary.zh: 全科医生在病人就诊时正在迅速推广一项新做法。然而，并非所有人都对此信服。

body.en:
Walk into a GP's room these days, and you might be asked something new: "Do you consent to me using an AI transcription tool?"

It's a question that could soon become routine, with AI scribes now used by roughly 40 per cent of Australian GPs, up from 22 per cent in August 2024, according to survey data from the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners (RACGP).

Dr Janice Tan, a spokesperson for RACGP's expert committee, said GPs and clinicians use AI scribes to transcribe conversations with patients, take automated notes, and summarise what was discussed.

"During the consult, they [the AI scribe] listen and produce a draft note afterwards," she told SBS News. "Many also draft referral and specialist letters, care plans, and sometimes a plain-English summary for the patient."

But she's clear that the software documents interactions — it doesn't decide care plans.

"A product that starts suggesting a diagnosis or treatment the clinician didn't state is no longer a scribe, and sits in a different regulatory category," she said.

But another expert said more safeguards are needed to protect patients — and the benefits aren't as clear-cut as they first appear.

For GPs, Tan said the appeal comes down to reduced burnout and more patient-centred care.

"There's less documentation after hours, which is a real driver of burnout and people leaving the profession," she said.

"The doctor is looking at you rather than the keyboard … there's more patient-centred consults, not quicker ones."

"The most underused benefit is the patient-facing summary … [which features] what we discussed, what changed, when to come back. That's valuable for anyone managing something complex, and for carers."

She also said it allows for "better and more consistent records", which are particularly helpful if you don't always see the same GP.

Andrew Cullen from the University of Melbourne's School of Computing and Information Systems agrees GPs are the clear winners — but is more cautious about what patients get out of it.

"GPs and clinicians love scribes, because they no longer need to take notes — so they can devote more time to their patients," he told SBS News. "However, for patients, the benefit is a lot less clear."

His main concern is 'hallucination' — when AI systems, including scribes, confidently make up facts. He cited a 2025 study which he said found "up to 20 per cent of notes made by AI scribes contained major errors".

title.en: The major citizenship ruling affecting Australians like Ophelia
title.zh: 影响奥菲莉亚等澳大利亚人的重大公民身份裁决

summary.en: A landmark court ruling in Australia is expected to alter the criteria and possibilities for citizenship claims for certain individuals within the country.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚一项具有里程碑意义的法院裁决，可能会重塑该国部分公民的公民身份申请条件和可能性。

body.en:
When Ophelia Bryant first travelled to Italy in 1986, she says she felt something she could not quite explain.

Her parents had been born in Italy, as had all four of her grandparents. They immigrated to Australia in 1955, where Bryant was born three years later.

Italy has remained a constant in her life, with Bryant returning more than a dozen times to visit relatives and reconnect with her family roots.

But when she began looking into whether she could formally claim Italian citizenship, she discovered her family history came with a legal complication.

Her parents became Australian citizens in 1961, when Bryant was a child, and later formally renounced their Italian citizenship.

Under a restrictive interpretation of Italy's citizenship laws, known as the 'minor issue', that could break the line of citizenship transmission.

Now, a landmark decision by Italy's highest court has changed that legal interpretation — and Bryant is "optimistic because that door may finally be open".

The so-called minor issue arose from conflicting interpretations of Italy's 1912 citizenship law.

One provision established that children born overseas to an Italian citizen could acquire Italian citizenship from birth.

Another was interpreted as meaning that when an Italian parent became a citizen of another country, their minor children could lose their Italian citizenship along with them.

That interpretation gained ground through Italian court decisions from 2023 onwards, leading to the rejection of citizenship-by-descent applications.

But in July, Italy's Supreme Court's United Sections, the court's highest panel for resolving conflicting legal interpretations, ruled that citizenship acquired at birth was not automatically lost when an Italian parent subsequently naturalised in another country.

Brisbane-based Italian lawyer Fabrizio Fiorino, who advises clients on Italian citizenship applications, said the decision effectively restores the previous interpretation of the law.

"It was not a change in a provision, but it was a change in the interpretation of rules," he said.

He told SBS News the ruling means people who were Italian citizens from birth cannot simply be considered to have lost that citizenship because their parents later became foreign citizens while they were minors.

For thousands of people whose citizenship applications were rejected on that basis, the decision could provide a pathway back.

Italy's interior ministry has since issued a letter instructing authorities to follow the Supreme Court's interpretation.
